AI GOVERNANCE / 01
Book a consultationService Brief — AI Governance Framework

AI governance built on whose data it is, not just what the system does.

A governance framework and operating model for organisations deploying AI — Copilot, Azure AI, generative tools, automated decisions — grounded in Te Mana Raraunga Māori Data Sovereignty principles and Te Tiriti o Waitangi, with a compliance layer that maps straight onto your Microsoft environment.

Book a consultation See what's included
The Gap

AI adoption is outrunning AI governance.

Copilot licences get switched on. Models get connected to live data. Meanwhile the questions that actually carry risk — who approved this, whose data is in it, what happens if it's wrong — are often answered after the fact, if at all.

 
01 Vendor AI tools go live with no cultural or legal review of the data feeding them.
02

Māori and Indigenous data sits inside systems with no rangatiratanga, no consent trail, no way back.

03

Boards ask "are we compliant?" and nobody owns a straight answer.

The Foundation

Six principles, non-negotiable.

Every recommendation in the framework is tested against Te Mana Raraunga's principles for Māori Data Sovereignty (2018) before it's tested against anything else — including the Microsoft roadmap.

Rangatiratanga
Authority

Māori hold decision-making authority over Māori data — what's collected, how it's used, and by whom.

Whakapapa
Relationships

Data carries its origins with it. Provenance and context travel with every dataset and model output.

Whanaungatanga
Obligations

Individual data rights are weighed against the rights of the collective they belong to.

Kotahitanga
Collective benefit

Systems are designed so Māori communities gain real, tangible benefit — not just the organisation.

Manaakitanga
Reciprocity

Dignity and consent come first. Free, prior and informed consent is a design requirement, not a checkbox.

Kaitiakitanga
Guardianship

Tikanga and mātauranga Māori shape how data is protected, accessed, and used — end to end.

The Engagement

What's included.

A governance framework you can put in front of a board, plus the operating detail to actually run it.

Structure

Governance roles & decision rights

An AI Governance Board, a Māori Data Governance Group, and clear ownership across platform owners, risk teams, and business units — so every AI decision has a named owner.

Risk

Risk & lifecycle management

Cultural, privacy, security, bias, and reputational risk mapped across the full AI lifecycle — from ideation through to retirement — with guardrails at each stage.

Platform

Microsoft ecosystem enablement

Configuration and compliance detail for Copilot, Purview, and Azure AI — data classification, access controls, audit logging, monitoring dashboards.

Assurance

Monitoring & reporting

Ongoing compliance checks, risk metrics, and quarterly governance reviews — the recurring service that keeps the framework alive after go-live.

Capability

AI & data sovereignty literacy

Training for executives and teams — AI literacy, Copilot fluency, and Māori and Indigenous data sovereignty grounding, delivered as workshops or briefings.

Delivery

An operating model, not a PDF

Escalation paths, approval workflows, and reporting lines defined clearly enough that governance survives contact with a busy Tuesday.

Optional Module

Working across borders? Add global Indigenous data sovereignty.

Activated only when a client's footprint calls for it — this module extends the framework to Indigenous data governance standards beyond Aotearoa.

  • CARE Principles — global Indigenous data standard
  • OCAP® Principles — Canada
  • AIATSIS Code of Ethics — Australia
  • Tribal Data Sovereignty — United States
  • Pacific Indigenous data governance frameworks
The Process

Four stages, start to steady-state.

01 — Assess

Where you stand

Audit current AI use, data flows, and exposure — including any Māori or Indigenous data already in play.

02 — Design

The framework

Governance structures, risk controls, and sovereignty principles tailored to your organisation and sector.

03 — Implement

In the platform

Controls configured directly in Copilot, Purview, and Azure AI — not left as policy on a shelf.

04 — Assure & train

Steady state

Ongoing monitoring, quarterly reviews, and literacy training keep the framework current as AI use grows.

Get Started

Let's build a framework your board — and your community — can stand behind.

Book a consultation Review the principles

Aligned with Te Mana Raraunga (2018), Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and — where engaged — CARE, OCAP®, AIATSIS, and Tribal Data Sovereignty standards.
